prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” HVAC company for everyone — it depends on your exact location, the problem, budget, and whether you need emergency same‑day service or a long‑term maintenance partner. I can help you find highly rated options nearby if you tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood. Meanwhile, here’s a concise plan and what to look for so you get a reliable tech and a fair price.

Quick steps
- Give me your ZIP or neighborhood and whether this is an emergency. I’ll list top-rated local companies and what reviewers say.
- Call 2–3 companies for estimates and compare price, availability, and warranties.
- Pick the one that is licensed, insured, transparent on price, and provides a written estimate and warranty.

How to choose a good HVAC company
- Licensing & insurance: Verify Arizona Registrar of Contractors license and general liability insurance.
- Certifications & experience: Look for NATE-certified techs and experience with your system brand.
- Reviews & reputation: Check recent Google, Yelp, and BBB reviews for consistent quality and responsiveness.
- Clear written estimate: Includes labor, parts, brand/model numbers, and total price. Watch for high-pressure sales.
- Warranties & guarantees: Ask about workmanship guarantees and parts warranties.
- Emergency & availability: If it’s 110°F outside, fast response time matters.
- Permits & code compliance: A reputable company will pull permits for major replacements.

Typical costs (very rough)
- Minor repairs/diagnostics: $75–$300 (diagnostic fee often applied to repair if you proceed)
- Refrigerant leak repair: $200–$1,000+ depending on parts and labor
- Capacitor/contactor/thermostat: $100–$600
- Compressor or major component: $1,500–$4,000+
- Full system replacement: $4,000–$12,000+ (depends on size and SEER rating)

Red flags / scam warnings
- Door‑to‑door “we were in your neighborhood” high‑pressure offers
- Asking for large cash up front, or no written contract
- Refusal to provide license/insurance or answer basic questions about parts/warranty
- Suggesting a “quick refrigerant top‑off” without diagnosing a leak

If you want, provide your ZIP code and a short description of the problem (no cool air, short cycling, noisy, smells, system age), and I’ll give a short list of well‑rated companies in your area plus a phone script and questions to ask when you call.
